articles.title: Why Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid reportedly told Josh Simmons to leave a Chiefs meeting after heated exchange
articles.summary: Josh Simmons’ difficult start to life with the Kansas City Chiefs has taken another turn after a reported confrontation with head coach Andy Reid during a
articles.body: Josh Simmons’ difficult start to life with the Kansas City Chiefs has taken another turn after a reported confrontation with head coach Andy Reid during a team meeting. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes also told the offensive tackle to leave the room, according to a report from NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport, cited by Bleacher Report. The incident reportedly happened Wednesday, when Reid challenged Simmons over his posture during the meeting. Simmons explained that he was dealing with back and hip pain. He later apologised to Reid and his teammates, but the episode has added another layer to his frustrating season.Josh Simmons’ exchange with Andy Reid led to his exitAccording to the report, Simmons was sitting with his feet raised in the offensive meeting room when Reid asked him to put them down. Simmons responded that his back and hips were aching, which made sitting that way more comfortable.Reid then told the young tackle to seek treatment from the team’s athletic trainers if he was experiencing pain. The exchange escalated to the point that Mahomes also told Simmons he should leave the meeting, according to the report. Simmons exited the room and later apologised to both Reid and his teammates.The reported disagreement was not simply about a player’s seating position. It put Simmons in a difficult spot as he tries to establish himself in Kansas City while dealing with an injury that has kept him off the field. Reid’s response also reflected the expectations inside a team meeting, where players are expected to follow the coach’s instructions even when they have concerns of their own.There is no reported indication that the incident alone led to Simmons’ subsequent roster move. The available account describes the exchange and his apology, but does not establish any further disciplinary action.Simmons’ injury setback leaves the Chiefs with another problemKansas City placed Simmons on injured reserve on Thursday, according to Bleacher Report. The 2025 first-round pick had already seen his rookie season cut short by a fractured wrist. A bulging disk in his back has prevented him from playing in 2026, leaving the team waiting for him to make meaningful progress in his recovery.Chiefs trainer Rick Burkholder offered a more detailed picture of that process this week. He said Simmons had been working hard and had improved enough to return to limited practice last week, but his rehabilitation had since stalled.“He worked diligently with my staff every day and has improved to point where he could return to practice in a limited capacity last week,” Burkholder said. “However, we feel like he's plateaued in the rehab process as he's trying to get to the final steps of recovery with the return to competition. He's just not there yet.”That is the more pressing issue for Kansas City. Simmons was drafted in the first round to address a key need on the offensive line, but the Chiefs have instead turned to undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson at left tackle. Simmons’ injured reserve placement means he will miss at least four more weeks, according to the report.For Simmons, the immediate challenge is to get healthy and return to the field. The reported meeting incident has drawn attention, but his recovery remains the central concern for a Chiefs team that still needs the young tackle to deliver on his potential.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: La NFL se estrena en París con Aaron Rodgers en plan estrella a sus 42 años
articles.standfirst: Los Pittsburgh Steelers derrotan por 16-10 a los New Orleans Saints en el Stade de France
articles.summary: Los Pittsburgh Steelers derrotan por 16-10 a los New Orleans Saints en el Stade de France
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers guió este domingo a los Pittsburgh Steelers al triunfo por 16-10 sobre los New Orleans Saints en el primer partido de temporada de la NFL en la historia disputado en París. En el encuentro, que se disputó sin contratiempos en el Stade de France, Rodgers, cuatro veces MVP de la temporada, pasó para 212 yardas y un envío de anotación. Con la victoria, tercera consecutiva, los Steelers se colocaron con cinco triunfos y dos derrotas en la cima de la división Norte de la Conferencia Americana, mientras que los Saints quedaron con marca de 2-5 en el tercer puesto del Sur de la Conferencia Nacional. La ofensiva de los Steelers tuvo un inicio dominante sobre la defensiva de los Saints, a la que arrastraron 51 yardas en ocho jugadas con Jaylen Warren como el ariete que se apuntó 43 de esas yardas, pero se atascaron dentro de la zona roja y se conformaron con un gol de campo de 28 yardas que convirtió Chris Boswell para tomar ventaja de 3-0. En el segundo cuarto, Tyler Shough movió al ataque de los Saints en una serie que recorrió 62 yardas para que Daniel Carlson empatara el partido 3-3 luego de conectar una patada de tres puntos de 38 yardas. El equipo de Pittsburh recuperó la ventaja (10-3) con un pase de Aaron Rodgers a las diagonales que atrapó Darnell Washington, en una serie en la que fue clave una conexión de Rodgers con DK Metcalf de 51 yardas que dejó a su equipo dentro de la yarda cinco del territorio de los Saints. Con este pase de anotación, Rodgers se convirtió en el tercer pasador con más envíos de 'touchdown' en la historia de la NFL, con 540, aún lejos de Drew Brees, segundo con más envíos a las diagonales, con 571, y Tom Brady, el primero, con 649. El equipo de Nueva Orleans volvió a establecer su ofensiva, que atravesó 51 yardas hasta la anotación de Devaughn Vele, quien atrapó un envío de Shough que igualó el juego 10-10. Los Steelers se fueron al descanso con ventaja de 13-10 luego de que Chris Boswell convirtiera un gol de campo de 47 yardas en el último segundo del periodo. En el inicio del tercer cuarto los Saints se comieron la mitad del reloj en una ofensiva que amenazaba con terminar en anotación, pero a 10 yardas de las diagonales Shough fue interceptado por Payton Wilson, acierto que el ataque de los Steelers convirtió en tres puntos más, 16-10, con un gol de campo de Boswell que significó la victoria. Antes del inicio de este partido, Roger Goodell, comisionado de la NFL, dijo que no tenía dudas de que la liga regresará a París con otro partido de temporada regular. Goodell lo afirmó a pesar de que la NFL canceló varias actividades con aficionados el sábado anterior debido a las protestas que la capital francesa ha sufrido de manera recurrente desde hace un par de semanas.

articles.title: NFL Paris 2026: Aaron Rodgers leads Pittsburgh Steelers past New Orleans Saints in first-ever game in France
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers beat the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in the first-ever NFL regular-season game to be played in Paris; Aaron Rodgers passes Peyton Manning for the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history
articles.body:
The four-time MVP quarterback surpassed Manning's tally of 539 touchdown passes with a first-half strike to tight end Darnell Washington and finished the game 19 of 30 for 212 yards as Mike McCarthy's Steelers improved to 5-2 on the year.

Saints quarterback Tyler Shough went 30 of 38 for 278 yards, a touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele and a second-half interception as Kellen Moore's side, honouring their deep-rooted French ties this week, dropped to 2-5.

Pittsburgh's Terrible Towels flew proudly while travelling Saints translated NOLA noise to Europe as the Stade de France welcomed 78,488 fans for the sixth of nine international games this season, Paris one of three first-time hosts for 2026 alongside Melbourne and Rio de Janeiro.

Civil unrest in France had dominated build-up to Sunday's game after what began as peaceful demonstrations had turned into violence and looting, resulting in the cancellation of fan events and prompting an increased security presence across the city.

Still, an undeterred crowd would serenade more NFL history with another electric atmosphere reflect of the league's reach overseas, albeit bolstered by a significant travelling party from both Pittsburgh and New Orleans.

Chris Boswell was a perfect three of three on field goals, while Saints counterpart Daniel Carlson was guilty of a costly miss.

Trailing 13-10 at the break, the Saints saw their immediate reply come up empty when Shough was intercepted by Payton Wilson to end a 14-play drive that had knocked a costly seven-and-a-half minutes off the clock.

Rodgers would later joke in his press conference about how Wilson intercepted him on a near-identical play during practice earlier in the week.

"I nearly took that one to the house," laughed Wilson.

Chase Young kept his team alive on the ensuing possession when the Saints sack leader swarmed Rodgers to stall the drive on third-and-10, Boswell coming out to kick a 39-yard field goal.

The Saints, though, were denied a chance to cut into Pittsburgh's lead again when Daniel Carlson missed a 52-yard field goal with 10 minutes remaining. Carlson had notably arrived in Paris on his own late this week, with his wife due to give birth back home.

Boswell had delivered the first-ever points scored in Paris with a 28-yard field goal at the end of Pittsburgh's opening drive, before giving his team a 13-10 lead with his 47-yard effort as time expired in the second quarter.

Carlson drew the Saints level at 3-3 with a 38-yard field goal after Shough had flipped the field with a 49-yard strike to Barion Brown.

Pittsburgh tight end Washington scored the first-ever touchdown in Paris when he treated the French crowd to a tinge of Randy Moss while out-muscling a helpless Kool-Aid McKinstry for a four-yard grab at the side of the end zone. His exhibition in bully ball would see Rodgers join Manning for the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history.

Rodgers himself had teed up the touchdown beautifully with a 51-yard strike to DK Metcalf after climbing the pocket and launching deep on the move to convert on third-and-14.

Shough capped his side's response with a one-yard touchdown pass to Vele inside the two-minute warning after the Saints had been stuffed at the one-yard line for three straight plays.

Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy: "I think the most important thing is you have a chance to travel as a team and the challenge of being on the road is always exciting, but this is special. I think everything that goes into this game, first time playing in France, and so it definitely brings a special feel to it. I think it's really good for your team; you have a chance to get on the road. It's been a joy to play here.

"I wouldn't say it (unrest in Paris) overshadowed the game, I know a lot of our team had families in France. I know everybody enjoyed Friday. With the uncertainty Saturday we stayed close to the hotel. France is a beautiful place. It's my first time here and I'd love the opportunity some day to come back and enjoy it."

Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers: "I've enjoyed the last two international games (Ireland and France), and then obviously London. For a long time in Green Bay we never got to go overseas because Lambeau is such an incredible home and they were never going to give up a home game and then we did in 2022. I've enjoyed it; I wish we could have enjoyed it both in Ireland and France for a little more time. It's great the game is growing."

Terron Armstead, former New Orleans Saints offensive tackle, on Sky Sports: "You definitely saw the difference between the two quarterbacks. Aaron Rodgers pretty much controlled the game. He was very solid, did nothing crazy and ultimately just took care of the ball. What it came down to was the Saints' inability to take care of the ball and score points when they got in the red zone. Turnovers will kill you every time."

Passing: Aaron Rodgers, 19/30, 212 yards, 1 TD

Rushing: Jaylen Warren, 18 carries, 101 yards

Receiving: DK Metcalf, 2 catches, 56 yards

Passing: Tyler Shough, 30/38, 278 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT

Rushing: Tyler Shough, 3 carries, 7 yards

Receiving: Alvin Kamara, 7 catches, 57 yards

articles.title: Malik Willis, Dolphins fend off Jets late to pick up first win of the season
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are now the only team in the NFL still without a win this fall.
articles.body:
At long last, Malik Willis and the Miami Dolphins won.

Willis and the Dolphins fended off a late push to beat the New York Jets 28-25 at MetLife Stadium on Sunday afternoon. The victory ends Miami's five-game losing skid to start the season. The win also brought the Dolphins out from the bottom of the league.

The Los Angeles Chargers are the only team in the league without a win.

Though it wasn't great, or even a complete game offensively, Willis and the Dolphins showed stretches of solid football — especially in the first half. They scored a touchdown on each of their first two drives of the afternoon, first on a 7-yard pass to Caleb Douglas and then on a 1-yard punch-in from Ollie Gordon. The opening touchdown was the first of Douglas' career.

The Dolphins pushed their lead to 14 points at the break. Willis scrambled into the end zone from 2 yards out in the final seconds of the second quarter to cap a 91-yard drive. It was easily Willis' best outing this season.

For some reason, that didn't carry over into the second half. Willis and the Dolphins stalled offensively for most of the third and fourth quarters. That left the door open for the Jets, who cut the deficit to a single score after an Omar Cooper Jr. touchdown grab in the third quarter. That was set up by a 60-yard reception he made earlier in the drive.

They should have tied the game in the fourth quarter, and got all the way to the goal line before the Dolphins came up with a huge stand. They stuffed the run twice and then sacked Geno Smith for a 12-yard loss on third down to force the field goal.

Finally, after completing only three passes in the second half, Willis found Douglas one last time. Willis dumped it off short to him on the left side, right before taking a huge hit in the backfield, and Douglass took off. He made it 63 yards up the sideline and into the end zone.

That still wasn't enough to seal the deal. The Jets got back within a field goal quickly, thanks to a Mason Taylor 12-yard touchdown catch and successful 2-point conversion. But the Dolphins quickly ended the game and converted a fourth-down run at midfield to kill the rest of the clock and escape with the three-point win.

Willis ended up going 14-of-21 passing for 208 yards with two touchdowns; all but four of those passes were completed in the first half. Gordon had 103 rushing yards and a score on 25 carries, and Greg Dulcich had 86 yards on five catches.

The victory was the first of head coach Jeff Hafley's career. The Dolphins hired Hafley to replace Mike McDaniel in January, marking Hafley's first head-coaching job in the league after his previous stint as the Green Bay Packers' defensive coordinator.

Smith went 23-of-30 passing for 287 yards with three touchdowns and an interception in the loss for the Jets (2-5). Braelon Allen had 104 yards on 17 carries, and Cooper had 115 yards and a score on his five catches. The Jets have lost five of their past six games, and will need a big turnaround if they are going to make any sort of playoff push in the back half of the season.

Similarly, the Dolphins still have a long way to go to salvage this season. It won't get any easier, either, with Drake Maye and the New England Patriots up next in Week 8. But finally winning a game, and beating a division rival in the process, is a great first step.

articles.title: Falcons LB Kendal Daniels, a week after scary neck injury, recovers fumble late to help lift Atlanta past San Francisco
articles.summary: Kendal Daniels was carted off the field last week after a scary neck injury he suffered against the Chicago Bears.
articles.body:
Kendal Daniels appears to be perfectly fine.

Daniels, just a week removed from a scary neck injury that forced him to be stretchered off the field , came up with a game-sealing fumble recovery on Sunday afternoon to lift the Atlanta Falcons past the San Francisco 49ers .

The Falcons were up by nine late at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, trying to fend off one last-ditch effort from the 49ers. With less than a minute left, San Francisco tight end George Kittle caught a wide open pass and was breaking to the middle of the field, seemingly putting the 49ers into scoring position.

But Jessie Bates dove for Kittle's legs and managed to just barely trip him up. As he was stumbling forward, Kittle lost the ball — which allowed Daniels to fly in and land on it untouched.

That secured the 29-20 win for the Falcons, and officially handed the 49ers their first loss of the season.

Daniels ended up leading the Falcons with a career-high 11 total tackles on Sunday, nine of which he did by himself. While the fumble recovery was the most important, he was a force for the Atlanta defense all afternoon. He even intercepted 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy late in the fourth quarter, which was one of four turnovers they forced all day.

Daniels, who the Falcons took in the fourth round of the NFL Draft out of Oklahoma, is now up to 40 total tackles this season.

But Sunday's outing came on the heels of what was a scary looking injury in their Week 7 matchup with the Chicago Bears. Daniels came flying in to try and tackle Bears tight end Colston Loveland, and he remained down on the field for roughly 10 minutes before being carted off.

But just days later, Daniels was back at practice and had been cleared to return.

"I scared a lot of people," Daniels said, via the Atlanta Journal-Constitution . "It was a scary play. I'm blessed to come out how I did, and it was a bang-bang play, but I'm happy I'm here."

The Falcons now sit at 3-4 on the season after Sunday's win. They'll take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers next week in Florida.

And Daniels, now with his terrifying neck injury clearly behind him, can keep pushing forward in what has been an already impressive rookie campaign.

articles.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen was asked about replacing QB Daniel Jones; here's what he said
articles.summary: Colts QB Daniel Jones turned in another poor performance, here's what coach Shane Steichen said about replacing him after Sunday's loss to Vikings
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones turned in another poor performance in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings , completing 13-of-22 passes for 108 yards with no touchdowns and a game-ending interception. He also took four sacks.

But Colts coach Shane Steichen said he has no plans to replace Jones as the starter.

"No, I haven't thought about a quarterback change," he said in his postgame news conference. "I have a ton of faith in Daniel. Our game plan was to go in and run the football and obviously, at the end, he had the interception; that happens."

Indianapolis Colts photos vs Minnesota Vikings in NFL Week 7

Steichen acknowledged the pass game "wasn't where we wanted it." Backup quarterback Anthony Richardson , who was charged with marijuana possession on Monday, Oct. 19, has not thrown a pass in a regular-season game since suffering a serious, freak eye injury prior to a game on Oct. 12, 2025.

Joel A. Erickson and Nathan Brown cover the Colts all season. Get more coverage on IndyStarTV and with the Colts Insider newsletter .

articles.title: Joe Burrow says Ja'Marr Chase fired up Bengals at halftime vs Ravens
articles.summary: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow said receiver Ja'Marr Chase was the one who fired up the team during halftime in Baltimore.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow said receiver Ja'Marr Chase was the one who fired up the team during halftime of the team's NFL Week 7 rout of the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium.

"We executed in the second half," Burrow told CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson after the game. "We called a great second half. We were able to complete some balls and find efficiency in the run game and make some plays. That's what we needed."

Wolfson asked Burrow what was said in the locker room during halftime.

Best Photos from Ravens vs. Bengals NFL Week 7 Matchup

"Ja'Marr went in there and got after everybody a little bit," Burrow said. "And (he) got everybody fired up. You know, that certainly plays a part. But at the end of the day, we just executed."

Chase finished the game with five catches for 62 receiving yards, and caught one of Burrow's four touchdown passes.

articles.title: Miami Dolphins no longer winless after defeating New York Jets
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins are no longer among the winless teams in the NFL. The Dolphins never trailed in a 28-25 victory over the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins are no longer among the winless teams in the NFL.

After never leading at any point in any game this season, the Dolphins (1-5) never trailed in a 28-25 victory Sunday over the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium.

Miami turned a 7-7 game into a 21-7 halftime lead before Chop Robinson capped the team's best defensive stand of the season in the fourth quarter and preserved the lead.

Miami then hung on to give Jeff Hafley the first victory of his NFL head coaching career.

Miami Dolphins hope for first NFL win at New York Jets

Miami's win means the Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) remain the lone winless team in the league. The Chargers were off Sunday.

How bad was it for the Jets (2-5)? A fan was shown with a paper bag over his head that read: "Not even Miami?"

Miami returns home Sunday, Nov. 1, to face New England (4-3). The Patriots are coming off a Thursday night loss at Chicago.

Here are five instant takeaways from the Dolphins' first win of the season:

Rookie receiver Caleb Douglas returns from injury with a big game

Caleb Douglas, a third-round draft pick from Texas Tech, played for the first time after suffering an ankle injury in Week 2 and recorded the first two touchdowns of his career, scoring on his only two catches.

Douglas, who started his college career at Florida, scored on the opening drive on a 7-yard pass from Malik Willis. Douglas then scored what became the game-winning touchdown with 4:44 remaining on a 63-yard catch-and-run in which he tip-toed the sideline around midfield as former Dolphins safety Minkah Fitzpatrick attempted to shove him out of bounds.

It took six games but Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley got his first win as an NFL head coach. And it could not have come in a better spot.

The game in the Meadowlands was 17 miles from Hafley's hometown of Montvale, N.J. His mom, brother and sister were in the stadium, as were about 30 other friends and family members. They all witnessed the biggest victory of Hafley's career.

The Dolphins looked like anything but one of two remaining winless teams in the NFL entering Week 7. They dominated early, leading 21-7 at the half and outgaining the Jets, 231-114, in the first 30 minutes with a very balanced offense. Miami then held on for the win.

"The offense did a great job in every one of their possessions," Hafley told CBS at halftime. "Malik is using his legs, he's throwing the ball well. We settled down on defense after we busted that first drive (allowing the Jets to drive down the field and tie the game at 7). We just got to come out and be consistent and keep doing what we're doing."

Hafley three-times went for a first down on fourth down and was 3-for-3. The biggest came at the end of the game after the two-minute warning when Willis got 2-yards with the ball on the Jets 49.

In the first half, Ollie Gordon's 1-yard touchdown on fourth down gave Miami a 14-7 lead, and Willis scrambled for 5 yards on 4th-and-2 from the Jets' 41, extending Miami's third TD drive.

Hafley was hired by GM Jon-Eric Sullivan, 10 days after Sullivan came to Miami. They knew each other well having worked together in Green Bay, Sullivan as the VP Player Personnel and Hafley the defensive coordinator. While they embarked on a very deliberate rebuild, no one knew how the season would unfold.

As CBS went to a commercial after Miami drove 76 yards on the game's opening drive for a touchdown, Foreigner's "Feels Like the First Time" was playing. The reason: It marked the first time Miami held a lead this season. The Dolphins were the only team entering Week 7 that had not led at any point in a game.

That lead, which came on a 7-yard pass from Willis to Douglas, lasted all of 2:16 as the Jets needed just four plays to drive 65 yards to tie the score. Miami regained the touchdown lead again on a 1-yard Gordon run with less than a minute to play in the first quarter. This time the lead held for good.

Malik Willis in control with zero turnovers

Willis had his best half with the Dolphins in the first 30 minutes and held steady in the second half. The five-year veteran entered the game with a 68.4 passer rating and had a first-half rating of 132.9 after completing 10-of-13 passes for 128 yards. He closed 14 of 21 for 208 yards, 2 touchdown passes and a 130.7 rating.

More importantly, Willis protected the ball. He entered with four interceptions and five fumbles. The Dolphins did not commit a turnover against the Jets. Early on, Willis received great protection, often times throwing from a clean pocket. Willis was sacked twice in the second half.

Chop Robinson, defense tightens late in the game

The Jets were 1-yard from completely erasing the Dolphins' two-touchdown lead before Miami's most impressive defensive stand of the season.

The Jets went from first-and-goal at the 1 to fourth down from the 15 after Chop Robinson chased down Jets quarterback Geno Smith for a 12-yard sack, forcing New York to settle for a field goal to make the score 21-17.

Miami got key tackles from Zach Sieler on first down and Josh Uche on second down, both for losses of 1-yard before Robinson's sack.

The Jets went 3-and-out on their next series and cut the Dolphins lead to three with a late touchdown and two-point conversion, but Miami was able to run out the clock.

T om D'Angelo is a senior sports columnist and reporter for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at tdangelo@pbpost.com.

articles.title: Where Titans land after loss vs Browns for NFL draft order
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans are in the race to get the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft after Week 7.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans went back to their losing ways Oct. 25 with a last-second, 27-24 home defeat against the Cleveland Browns, moving them up to second in the standings for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

A week after their first win of the season, 26-20 against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 18, the Titans fell to 1-6 and moved from third to second in terms of where they currently are in the NFL draft order, per tankathon . The Titans last held the No. 1 pick in 2025.

According to tankathon.com , the Los Angeles Chargers (0-6), who did not play this week, would have the top pick based on their strength of schedule, which is the weakest among the worst teams in the NFL. The Miami Dolphins (1-5) picked up their first win of the season Oct. 25 against the Jets, but their strength of schedule is better than the Titans'.

Inside Titans vs Browns. Cam Ward, Jeffery Simmons and our best photos

Tennessee chose quarterback Cam Ward out of Miami with the first pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.

Here's the updated first-round order for the 2027 NFL Draft as Week 7 results come in. The draft order is according to Tankathon , which calculates strength of schedule differently from the NFL:

LA Chargers (0-6) .538 strength of schedule

Cleveland Browns (via Rams) (2-4) .524 SOS

Dallas Cowboys (via Packers) (4-2) .519 SOS

NFL Draft order is decided by the reverse order of each team's finish in the regular season and postseason.

The team with the worst record gets the No. 1 pick. Every pick after that, through pick 20, is determined by regular-season records from worst to best.

Should teams have identical records, the first tiebreaker is strength of schedule, meaning the team whose opponents had the worst combined winning % receives the higher pick.

If that number is identical, the second tiebreaker is division/conference, meaning head-to-head games, common opponents, strength of victory.

The final tiebreaker, should the first two not work, is a coin toss.

Who are the 2027 NFL Draft top prospects?

ESPN's Mel Kiper's top 10 prospects as of Oct. 15, are:

Would the Titans take another quarterback if they have the first pick in the NFL Draft?

That doesn't seem likely, but with 10 games remaining, the Titans will learn more about Cam Ward.

Side note: Five of Mel Kiper's top 10 prospects for the 2027 draft are quarterbacks, though Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith tops the list.

Side note II: Tankathon's latest mock draft Tankathon's mock draft has the Titans taking Texas edge Colin Simmons with the third overall pick..

Would the Titans opt for a receiver with top pick?

Taking a receiver and giving Ward some ,more tools with which to work would make sense. Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith, considered the best receiver prospect who is draft eligible, could help in Ward's development.

Would the Titans trade the first pick in the NFL Draft?

If stacking talent is the plan, trading the pick for players and/or more picks could speed up the Titans' rebuilding process.

Teams have traded first pick in the NFL Draft 13 times since 1967, when the common draft era began.

Cam Ward, Tennessee Titans QB in second season, No. 1 pick in 2025 NFL Draft

How many times have the Titans made No. 1 overall pick in NFL draft?

The Titans/Oilers have had the first overall pick in the NFL Draft three times.

Would the Titans draft Arch Manning with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft?

While another quarterback named Manning playing for a football team in Tennessee would be cute for a movie script, the reality is, Texas quarterback Arch Manning, nephew of former Tennessee Vols quarterback Peyton Manning, has done nothing to prove himself worthy of being the top overall pick.

Paul Skrbina is a sports enterprise reporter covering the Predators, Titans, Nashville SC, local colleges and local sports for The Tennessean. Reach him at pskrbina@tennessean.com and on the X platform (formerly known as Twitter) @paulskrbina .

articles.title: How to watch Sunday Night Football, Chiefs face Seahawks
articles.summary: The undefeated Kansas City Chiefs take on the defending Super Bowl champs Seattle Seahawks.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs put their unbeaten record on the line when they travel to Seattle to face the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks on "Sunday Night Football."

Entering Week 7 of the NFL season, the Chiefs were one of only three undefeated teams. The others were the San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings .

Quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs (5-0) will take on Seattle (3-3) and the 12s (formerly known as the 12th Man) at Lumen Field, one of the loudest stadiums in the NFL on "Sunday Night Football" on Oct. 25 on NBC.

The Chiefs are coming off a 22-6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 6. Seattle lost to the Denver Broncos , 14-17.

The Seattle Seahawks roster features linebacker Tyrice Knight , No. 48, a former UTEP Miner.

Knight, who serves mostly in a rotational and backup role, had five solo tackles and three assists in the Seahawks' last game, a 14-17 loss to the Denver Broncos last week.

Knight has been in the NFL for three years. He was selected by the Seahawks in the fourth round of the 2024 NFL draft. He was part of the Seahawks Super Bowl LX championship team last year.

Knight is a graduate of Lake Gibson High School in Lakeland, Florida.

Kansas City Chiefs coach Andy Reid is former UTEP offensive line coach on the record-winning Miners football team of 1988 .

What channel is Sunday Night Football on?

The "Sunday Night Football" game between the Seahawks and Chiefs can be seen on NBC.

articles.title: Browns win on walk-off field goal for second straight week, defeating Titans 27-24
articles.summary: For the second consecutive week, Deshaun Watson led a game-winning drive finished off by a field goal as time expired from Andre Szmyt.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns won their second consecutive game on a final drive and walk-off field goal. Andre Szmyt kicked a 32-yarder as time expired for a 27-24 win over the Tennessee Titans.

Cleveland's Week 7 victory follows a 13-10 win against the Baltimore Ravens, which also ended on a Szmyt field goal with no time remaining. That kick was from 37 yards, completing a comeback from a 10-point deficit .

Deshaun Watson threw for 308 yards, completing 25 of 36 passes with 1 interception. He completed all three of his passes on the Browns' final drive, including a 36-yard catch-and-run by tight end Harold Fannin.

KC Concepcion notched 8 receptions for 129 yards, while Quinshon Judkins rushed for 96 yards on 17 carries.

With the win, the Browns improve to 5-2 and are tied for first place in the AFC North with the Pittsburgh Steelers, who defeated the New Orleans Saints 16-10 earlier on Sunday in Paris.

Titans nearly took early two-touchdown lead

Tennessee scored touchdowns on their first two possessions, helped by an interception by Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson. The Titans opened by moving 65 yards in six plays, finished off with a 15-yard pass from Cam Ward to Carnell Tate followed by a 36-yard touchdown run by Tony Pollard.

Following an interception by Cor'Dale Flott on Cleveland's first drive, Pollard scored his second TD four plays later with a 10-yard rush.

Tennessee nearly had a two-touchdown lead after its defense forced a three-and-out toward the end of the first quarter. After advancing 53 yards on 11 plays, Pollard appeared to have his third TD on a 3-yard rush up the middle. However, the play was reviewed and Pollard's knee was ruled to be down before the ball crossed the goal line.

With three plays from the 1-yard line, the Titans could not punch the ball in for a score. Ward was stopped on a push up the middle, then was sacked on the next play. With a fourth-and-goal, Titans coach Robert Saleh opted to go for the TD but Pollard was stopped on an inside run by linebacker Winston Reid.

Both teams exchanged turnovers on their next respective possessions with Fannin fumbling for Cleveland and Denzel Ward getting an interception for the Browns on the next play.

Cleveland then tied the score at 14-14 with a 78-yard drive highlighted by 21-yard and 32-yard completions from Watson to Concepcion. Judkins finished off the series with a 6-yard TD run. The Browns took the lead on their next possession on a 28-yard field goal by Szymt.

The Titans got a game-tying field goal on a 29-yarder from Joey Slye with 8:41 remaining in the fourth quarter. But Cleveland took the lead on its next possession, finishing off a 71-yard series with Watson running 9 yards for the score.

Tennessee responded with a touchdown drive of its own with Cam Ward completing passes of 14 yards, 26 yards and 18 yards before Pollard got his third TD of the game on a 1-yard run.
